questions.question: What does the partial derivative $\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{f}}{\partial x_j}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$ measure?

The change in $\boldsymbol{f}$ when only the $j$-th coordinate is nudged.
The distance from $\boldsymbol{x}_0$ to the boundary of $\boldsymbol{E}$.
The value of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at every point of $\boldsymbol{E}$.
questions.explanation: $\partial\boldsymbol{f}/\partial x_j$ measures the change in $\boldsymbol{f}$ when only the $j$-th coordinate is nudged, holding the others fixed.
questions.source_support: Interpretation of partial derivative.

option_explanations: Changing all coordinates equally is a directional derivative along $(1,\ldots,1)$, not a partial.
The distance to the boundary is unrelated to a partial derivative.
A partial derivative is a local rate of change, not the value at every point.
